_description: The fighters lab's own numbers (tools/nn/fighters, docs/en/training/fighters_lab.md). Everything else comes from the game's database through the simulator's params (config/nn/game_rules.json, units.json) and its rules (config/nn/sim.json). Outside tools/nn/sim and config/nn on purpose: the lab does not change the simulator's version.

cells.why: the neighbour search (cells.py): a man sees every man within cell_m (3 x 3 cells round his own) - the reach 2.5 m (entity_action_attack_formed_combat_distance) + the largest body radius of our roster 0.9 (wolf rats) is 3.4; cap: men a cell holds at most (the densest close order, Empire infantry 1.48 x 1.6 m, ~5.5 a cell; a melee crush ~2x); hash: the cell table per battle (a power of 2)

standoff.why: MEASURED, not a rule of the game (none found in CA's material, the database or the community): how close a man in a fight stands to the enemy man he fights. The probes' soldiers' places once a second (reform, reform2, damaged, dmgmelee, wave, armour: 48 lanes, build/charge-probe/runs; shape.py front_gap: the median nearest-enemy distance of the 15 men nearest the enemy) - 0.98 / 1.14 / 1.32 / 1.51 / 1.91 / 2.24 / 2.26 / 2.39 m at 0-1 / 1-3 / 3-5 / 5-10 / 10-20 / 20-40 / 40-90 / 90-240 s after contact: d(t) = steady - (steady - start) exp(-t / tau), t the pair's seconds in melee (the younger of the two units' melee clocks, as the simulator's melee.wave). The men within reach of the enemy (and so the blows) follow from it; they are what the lab is checked by.

move.front_only_why: only a man of the formation's front rank (its foremost places; after an about-face the old back rank) with an enemy man in reach takes the standoff from him; the men behind keep their places (they still strike whatever is in their reach). With every man in reach closing on an enemy, the second rank pushed the first into the enemy: the probes' men within reach 34-45 against the game's 19 at 20-40 s after contact, the fronts 1.1-1.4 m apart against 2.3 (build/fighters/probes_a.json).
move.front_anchor_why: a formation keeps its ranks behind its fighting front: its places shift along its facing by the mean way its men with an enemy in reach stand off their own places (at most 3 m; back to 0 by half a step once none fights). Without it the front men could not step back to the standoff - the men behind them held them - and the fronts parted slower than the game's (front gap 1.43 / 1.78 m against 1.97 / 2.32 at 10-20 / 20-40 s; men within reach 40 / 34 against 27 / 19).
move.in_reach_only_why: only a man with an enemy man within his reach (the one he strikes) takes his standoff; the men behind keep their places (pushed back by the bodies in front). With every man within reach + the tether closing on an enemy, the second rank kept pushing the first into the enemy: the probes' men within reach 45 against the game's 19 at 20-40 s after contact (build/fighters/probes_a.json).
move.why: a man walks to his place in the formation (his file and rank, re-formed as men fall: the man behind steps up, the file closes up) at his unit's run speed relative to the unit's centre; in a fight he stands at the standoff from the enemy he fights, at most the database's entity_action_attack_formed_tether_distance (2.0 m) from his place; bodies (the database's radius) do not overlap. A formation that turns about (more than 90 deg in a step) swaps its ranks and files, as the game's about-face in place (the simulator's turn rule).

melee.why: a man's attack interval (the passport's) runs after a hit, a miss costs the simulator's melee.miss_s (CA Feature Focus #2: the interval runs after a blow); his clock runs only while an enemy is within his reach, so a man's first blow of the battle is at once (the first strike) and a unit coming back into a fight brings no new burst (the recontact probe: the second contact's first 3 s 0.24-1.35 of the steady rate, the first 2.87).
melee.blow_share_why: MEASURED, the lab's one open number (no rule found): a man within reach of an enemy man lands blows at this share of the database formula's rate p / (p x interval + melee.miss_s) x hit. The probes' soldier places and health (reform, reform2, damaged, dmgmelee, wave, armour, defender, fresh, meleeorders: 116 lane-sides one on one, build/charge-probe/runs), the game's HP lost a second by a unit over its striker's men within 3.15 m of it, against the formula's per-man rate: 0.38 / 0.35 / 0.32 / 0.36 / 0.36 / 0.30 at 2-5 / 5-10 / 10-20 / 20-40 / 40-90 / 90-240 s after contact (0.63 at 0-2 s: the first strike), by pair 0.2-0.65 (spearmen and halberdiers 0.2-0.3, greatswords and stormvermin 0.45-0.65; swordsmen v clanrats 0.29-0.32, 40 lanes). The simulator's rectangle carries the same gap in its fighting_files 0.5 (half the files in contact strike). What the game does with the rest is not known: candidates - the matched-combat animations (the database's matched_combat_*_percentage) holding both men, the attack animation's own time, men in reach that do not attack. A blow lands with this chance (the clock runs as for a swing).

knock.invulnerable_why: a man lying (knocked down) strikes nobody, nobody strikes him and no projectile or blast takes his health: the simulator's magic.knock reading (build/magic/probe2.md: lone men under the spells - with it the twin's damage 0.85 / 1.38 of the game, without 1.39 / 3.66) and the community (knocked-down infantry outlive what would kill them: steamcommunity WH3 'Realistic Charge' comments). Checked man by man on the knock probe (magic battle 6, build/magic/runs/20261016-211346, knockdata.py): of the men thrown, none died lying - 0 deaths in 778 man-seconds lying, while the men up near the strikes died at 0.005-0.020 a second (~11 deaths expected); the swordsmen in melee with clanrats, 31 of 106 thrown by Warp Lightning, took 20 / 13 HP a second off the clanrats 3-6 / 6-12 s after the strike against the control lane's 48 / 33 (the strike killed some of them too).

throw.why: how far the impact throws a man knocked back or down: median_m x exp(N(0, sigma_log)), at most max_m. MEASURED, no database number: the knock probe (magic battle 6, build/magic/runs/20261016-211346; soldiers' places every 0.1 s, each man followed, tools/nn/fighters/knockdata.py) - his move from his place before the strike to where he first stops, median / p10 / p90: Searing Doom on clanrats 3.26 / 2.29 / 6.04 m (208 men thrown of 537 in 4 strikes), on skavenslaves 3.20 / 2.27 / 7.24 (197 of 421), Warp Lightning on swordsmen 2.97 / 1.35 / 9.02 (70 of 244), on swordsmen in melee 2.80 / 1.58 / 4.74 (45 of 165); the same for both spells and every target, so one distribution (sigma from p10-p90 of Searing Doom: ln(6 / 2.3) / 2.56); the direction mostly away from the strike (cosine with the line from it: median 0.5-0.7); the control lane (no cast) had no strike. The old '1.5-3 m' (1 s places) held the men's ordinary moves.

missile.why: projectiles a battle traced per step at most (the rest wait for the next step), the points along a projectile's low path searched for bodies (cells.cell_m apart from the landing point back towards the shooter: 6 x 3.6 = 21.6 m; a flat shot's longer low path is cut there), projectiles a man looses per step at most
